# SHA-256 reduced to 39 steps: ordinary collision by the transplanted pair with two released state words (k = 4) on the fibre h4 = 0x3cc9eebe; the list generated by rule at import, the W17 condition solved on 18-bit prefixes by a generic counted pass

This entry is mitchuski's refile of 9054e0c4 (our w16, returned not_evaluable: its mate term had no organizer execution) on Jbenisek's ae2d3c1c (credited; itself a derivative of our 0b62ed88 with 0xplemonade's a3eb4a8a screen, credited). From ae2d3c1c it keeps the program, the screen, the screened whole-window H6 method and the fourth-decimal ceiling (from b7de1d07); it does not use ae2d3c1c's tail. Changes: (1) trials are F8-passing entries, 10701.9 per distinct claw, the one-sided 99% lower bound on 10,000 F9 claws of 80 screened windows, and K = 10,369 from 124 screened windows (ae2d3c1c's 60 and 64 more, declared before running); (2) the entries tail is priced at 2^-74.4783, the lower of the pooled and class-01 means of the 14 organizer-executed runs r39-mate-01..14 (Section 8); (3) a key succeeds on the union of its F8-passing mates' tails; an exhaustive enumeration of rows 18-19 shows a mate can pass row 19 only if the hit's W3 lies in a small explicit set (empty for 14 of the 20 offsets, at most 120,832 of 2^32 values for the others), and under the named premise H-W3-uniform, tested by the organizer on 1,888 hits (none in the set), eps/2 = 0.000099; without the premise the price would be 94.1648 (Section 7); (4) mu_D from the screened claws and co-hits on 65,536 w; (5) memory corrected by 96 bytes for the screen's state. The manifest is r39-transplant-claw, r39k4-window-small and r39-mate-01..14. Divisor 1 - 0.073047; windows B = 2^76.386613; total charged work 2^94.068209; time 94.0683; memory 2^20.0000. Base text below that speaks of ae2d3c1c's or 0b62ed88's own measurements is theirs (CITED).

History, CITED (0b62ed88, the keys-only form of this attack): 0b62ed88 refiled f429192b: the second-order term no longer rests on any window-moment reduction; it is bounded for any correlation by a cap of 1,024 evaluated claws per window and the measured maximum within-claw co-hit rate over every listed key (Section 7). It also refiles 209b4410: its time is priced by a second-order Bonferroni bound over ALL W17 key hits of a window, on designated-mate events: no hit is selected or ordered, every hit enters symmetrically, and the bound holds for any dependence between the tails of different hits (Section 7). The number sits next to 209b4410's but comes from a different derivation in which no hit is ordered or selected. Trials are distinct keys, with no premise on how the tails of a key's mates depend on each other (it also refiles 9a255e58). It is our w13 program (the line of 837b7139 and 089cd791) with one lever: the k = 4 list is re-based from the advice fibre h0 = 0x36faf0de to the fibre h4 = 0x3cc9eebe, and it is generated at import by a rule instead of being decoded from a shipped recipe. On the new fibre the list has 9,701,592 entries in 728 classes (3,462,264 distinct (a2, kappa) keys, 200 kappa groups, 62,400 distinct 18-bit prefixes), against 821,520 entries in 256 classes on h0. The walk constant c9 and the F9 constant C9 shift by h4 - h0 = 0x05cefde0; nothing else of the construction moves (Section 2.3). A trial is a distinct (a2, kappa) key with at least one listed entry passing F8 in a claw passing F9 (Section 7). Counting every hit follows a7b383d1 (credited). The list is Jbenisek's construction of f92b8068 continued to a new fibre; the walk, claw filters and tail replica are the line of 3aa063d1 (Jbenisek, dariolina, sraiw, newjordan). The work cap is measured on 60 screened full windows of the shipped attack path (Section 7, Appendix B); this entry adds 64 screened windows on the same path (Appendix C), so K comes from 124, and measures the trial count on 10,000 F9 claws of 80 screened full windows (Section 7).

Labels: MEASURED = run by us with the shipped program's counters or with the named tool; DERIVED = arithmetic from stated numbers; CITED = measured and published by the named earlier entry.

## 1. Target and output
- **Target.** `sha256-r39-prefix-v1`: SHA-256 with the first 39 steps in every compression, standard IV, FIPS 180-4 padding, feed-forward, all 256 output bits.
- **Output.** Two distinct 128-byte messages M0 || M1 and M0 || M1': the same random first block M0, second blocks with M1' = M1 + DL (word-wise modular, differences in words 8..12). Equal lengths, identical padding block. Ordinary collision.
- **Claim.** time_log2 = 94.0683, memory_log2_bytes = 20.0000, preprocessing_log2 = 43, advice 160 bytes = 2^7.32193, success probability 0.39. The time is total charged work (work cap, one-time setup, 2^43 preprocessing), ceiled at the fourth decimal; the memory is the peak over the phases of the run, 1,013,609 bytes, plus 32,768 bytes of headroom, claimed at 2^20.

## 2. The construction
**2.1 Advice.** The 39-step semi-free-start pair of 5f8e6192 (CV_PUB, MP_PUB, M_PUB; 160 bytes), on the characteristic of ePrint 2026/1120 Tables 21 and 23 (CITED from 293ca62c and 38912d66). No recipe is shipped: the advice is the 160-byte pair only.

**2.2 The transplant, k = 4.** As in w13: fix A[8..11], E[12..15] and W12..W15 to the advice values; for any cv and (a0, a1, a2, a3) = A[4..7] the words W0..W11 follow (`k4_words`). W9 = C - a1 + h4(a2, a3) with h4 = MAJ(A8, a3, a2) - CH(E12, E11, E10), E10 = a2 + t(a3), E11 = a3 + c11; W10 = kappa(a3) - a2; W11 depends on a3 only; W0 and W1 do not depend on (a2, a3).

**2.3 The fibre is a parameter.** On any fibre h4(a2, a3) = h, W9 = C - a1 + h is one value per claw, F9 stays a per-claw test, and W16 = s1(W14) + W9 + s0(W1) + W0 is one value per claw. Taking h = FIB = 0x3cc9eebe instead of the advice's h0 = 0x36faf0de shifts the walk constant c9 and the F9 constant C9 by K4_HD = FIB - h0 = 0x05cefde0 (computed by the program from the advice). A claw of the shifted walk map then gives W16 = g for every entry of the new list. The advice (a2, a3) itself is not on the new fibre, so the base variant is not a trial and its path is removed from `claw()`; the transplant-claw experiment no longer claws the advice (an h0 claw). MEASURED on the built program (build/e2e15.py, from w15/tools/check15s.py): all F9 claws of windows 1000 and 1014 of the shipped program x 20 listed entries each, 35,940 (claw, entry) cases: W1 = u, W16 = g, W9 = C9 + HD - a1 in F9, both messages on the advice trail through step 16, the advice states after step 17 at a W17 hit; failures none.

**2.4 What remains after a claw.** Per claw: W9 in F9. Per entry: W8 in F8 (density 9/128), and W17 = advice value; then the tail (Section 8). Two entries with the same a2 and kappa (mates) pass or fail W17 together; they differ in a3, hence in W11, W3..W8 and every tail word.

**2.5 The list by rule (MEASURED and DERIVED).**
- Classes: a3 = (E11adv XOR m) - c11 for every submask m of CUBE = 0xf74400da (14 bits, 16,384 masks), kept when W11C - a3 lies in F11: 1,536 candidates. CUBE is the OR of the E11 masks of the 728 classes of the exhaustive enumeration; the rule R2 of our list-ceiling note (E11 AND 0x08b81020 fixed) holds on the whole cube because the two masks are disjoint.
- Entries of a class: every a2 with (R3) h4(a2, a3) = FIB, (R4) W10 = kappa(a3) - a2 in F10, (R5) bit 30 of E10 equal to bit 30 of E11.
- **The rule set equals the exhaustive list.** enum15 scans all 2^32 values of a3 and checks every candidate entry on the real two-message trail at the advice point and three random points (0 mixed verdicts, 0 failures of every identity it checks; 9,701,592 valid entries in 728 classes). build/rule15.c generates the rule set and compares it with that list as sorted (a3, a2) sets: equal; at h0 the same rule gives exactly the 821,520-entry list of f92b8068.
- F10 is a set of bit conditions on W10 (D10 = 0xc0000000, T10 = 0x087ff000): w2^w13 = 1, w9^w26 = 1, w15 = w19, and either w30 = 1, or w30 = 0 with w3^w14 = w10^w27 = w31 = 1^w16^w20. Checked over all 2^32 values: 301,989,888 members, 0 mismatches.
- **Generator.** A bit-serial automaton over a2 (the fibre's carry and borrow, the borrow of kappa - a2, the captured W10 bits, the F10 branch) is solved backwards, bit-sliced over 256 candidate classes per 256-bit word (`_k4fe`); then a depth-first search with exact pruning lists the 18-bit prefixes of each class (`_k4lf`). Classes are taken in kappa order, and a group's prefix set becomes 18 bit planes per block of 256 lanes when the next group begins (`_k4fin`). One sample entry per group is kept for the planted checks.
- **Table.** 200 kappa groups, 728 classes (at most 8 per group), 62,400 prefixes in 300 blocks (at most 1,024 prefixes per group). MEASURED: group by group, the prefix sets built at import equal those of the exhaustive list, and every sample entry satisfies the rule. Counts asserted at import.

## 3. The W17 pass
**3.1 The equation.** As in w13: s0(y) = y + r with y = a2 + w and r = kd + W17 - u - w; the low 18 bits of y determine the other 14, and 18 bit checks remain.

**3.2 The pass (`k4q`).** The routine of w13, unchanged except two lines (Section 3.4). Per evaluated F9 claw: spill and restore (624), a1 and w (55), the 18 constant words (54); per group 110; per block 403. **K4_PASS = 733 + sum over the 200 groups of (110 + 403 x blocks) = 143,633, the same for every claw**, asserted at import. A survivor costs 711 plus 563 per class of its group tested: at most 711 + 563 x 8 = 5,215. A key hit tests the classes of its group as mates: at most 8 x (560 + 2 x 2,812) = 49,472.

**3.3 Same hits.** A listed key satisfies W17 in a claw if and only if its prefix lane survives and the scalar test accepts it. MEASURED by the gate on 6 real F9 claws of the shipped program's windows: for each of the 200 groups a planted key (the group's sample entry, its W17 placed as the target) is found by the pass, and the counted cost is the group's pass cost plus 711 + 563 x (classes tested) per survivor. The organizer experiment repeats it for all 200 groups on the first F9 claw of each window (Section 11).

**3.4 Changes against w13.** (i) The fibre: c9, C9 shifted; k4q's W9 reference is the claw's own W9, C9 + HD - a1, not the advice's; the mates of a key hit are the classes of its group, not the 4,096 submasks of 0xf1c000da. (ii) The list by rule: no recipe literal, no inflate reader, no decoder; the per-key diagnostic runs over the entries of every 50th group (four groups) and only in the experiment modes. (iii) The walk table: 97 x 1,024 = 99,328 slots of 40 bits, 15,520 words, the largest table under 2^20 with the other rows of Section 6. The slot of a 25-bit distinguished value r is (97 r) >> 15 = ((r << 6) + (r << 5) + r) >> 15 through the counter; 2^15 / 97 = 338 < 512, so slot and the 9 check bits determine r. Keep-longer rule as in w13.

**3.5 Routine by routine against w13** (ae2d3c1c's screen, Section 3.6, also changes `Attack.__init__` and `Attack.window_setup` and adds `k4_scr`; nothing else) (every routine of the source compared; module lines with constants are listed in Section 5). Changed: `consts` (c9 + K4_HD); `Attack.base_setup` (only C9, shifted, is left); `Attack.claw` (the base-variant path removed; check mode asserts the claw's W9 against a listed entry); `Attack.hit` (slot (97 r) >> 15 and its check); `P` (WDIG of 15,520 words); `k4q` (the claw's W9; mates among the group's classes); `k4f` (the diagnostic over the four groups of `_k4ind`); `_k4fin` (planes of one group from its prefix set); `k4_budget` (C_W, the entries tail and the second-order divisor; Section 5); `_e1` (transplant-claw: advice checks and the fibre checks per group; random transplants with a listed entry); `_k4e` (no base F8 count; the acceptance constants). Removed: `_w3gen`, `_k4c1`, `_sm`. Added: `_k4st`, `_k4fe`, `_k4lf`, `_k4cls`, `_k4build`, `_k4ind`, `h4ok`. Every other routine is byte-identical to w13's. This entry against 0b62ed88: `P` (SCREEN = 1, KCAP = 679, KCAP0 = 710 for the screen-off path, DTRY = 8,192), `k4_scr` (added), `Attack.__init__` (the screen flag), `Attack.window_setup` (the screen in the draw loop, Section 3.6), `K4_OPS_PER_CLAW`, `k4_budget` and the import assertion (Section 5), `_k4e` (the four asserted windows run with the screen off; trial 0 adds one screened window, Section 11).

**3.6 Pre-generation screen (credited to 0xplemonade's a3eb4a8a; its masks, threshold, KCAP = 679 and DTRY = 8,192 unchanged).** Each drawn first block's chaining value is scored before kernel generation: from `consts5` of the CV (cw, eb, P, R; 4 ops to pack), S = 3 pop(R & 0x00F27618) + 2 pop(R & 0x7F0D89E6) + 2 eb[1] + eb[2] + P[31] - pop(P & 0x1FFFFFFE), charged 183 ops per draw, a3eb4a8a's counted figure, kept here as a conservative charge above an explicit v5 form of at most 65 ops: with A = pop(R & 0x00F27618), B = pop(R & 0x7F0D89E6), C = pop(P & 0x1FFFFFFE), each count is the SWAR sequence x -= (x >> 1) & 0x55555555 (3); x = (x & 0x33333333) + ((x >> 2) & 0x33333333) (4); x = (x + (x >> 4)) & 0x0f0f0f0f (3); x += x >> 8 (2); x += x >> 16 (2); x &= 63 (1), 15 ops, so 3 counts plus 3 input masks = 48; eb[1], eb[2], P[31] extracted in 5; 3A, 2B, 2eb[1] in 4; the nonnegative S + 28 = 3A + 2B + 2eb[1] + eb[2] + P[31] + (28 - C) formed and compared, branch included, in at most 8. The program's host bit count, bin().count('1'), evaluates the same predicate; it is not a charged unit op, and the 183 charged ops per draw exceed the 65. A block with S > 5 is discarded (3 more ops) and the next block is drawn (its draw and first-block compression charged as before); a kept block goes to the unchanged exact kernel gate, which now accepts at most 679 records (KCAP; 710 in the base). A window stops after 8,192 discarded draws or 32 rejected generations, every charge counted. The screen consumes no randomness. Its effect on work enters the price only through the re-measured window totals (H6, Appendix B) and C_W; its effect on the window law and the trial count is the new premise H1-screen (Section 10).

## 7. Success probability and the cap
- **Trials (this entry).** A trial is a listed entry passing F8 in a claw passing F9. Mates of a key (the entries with the same a2 and kappa) share W17 and differ in a3, hence in W11, W3..W8 and every tail word from W18 on (Section 2.4). When a key hits W17 the program tests every class of its group, so every mate passing F8 is compressed. Let T_j be the event that entry j's pair collides along the advice differences (the event the tail replica counts) and U_k the union of T_j over the F8-passing mates of key k; the key succeeds on U_k. Second-order Bonferroni inside the key: P(U_k) >= sum_j P(T_j) - sum over mate pairs i < j of P(T_i and T_j); the pair term is bounded below (the mate term); no independence between mates is assumed.
- **Count: 10701.9 per distinct claw (screened windows, MEASURED).** By the rule declared before the panel ran (w17/panel/PREDECLARED.txt): the first 125 F9 claws (arrival order) of each of the 80 screened windows this entry ran (802000-802015 and 802060-802123; 10,000 claws, one batch per window); F9 claws per window from all 124 windows (ae2d3c1c's 60 and this entry's 64): 902.524 (s.e. 2.636); C_W = 57,012.41. The listed entries passing F8 number 681,102.5 per F9 claw (s.e. 762.6 from the 80 batch means; per-claw s.d. 70,410); trials per distinct claw = 681,102.5 x 902.524 / 57,012.41 = 10782.064 (s.e. 33.728); one-sided 99% lower bound with t(79) = 2.374: 10701.979, priced as 10701.9. Counted by w15/tools/f8count.exe over the exhaustive list. The same claws have 575,302.5 distinct keys with an entry in F8 per F9 claw (1.1839 entries per key); its one-sided 99% upper bound, printed upward 576,819, is mu_D of the cross-claw term.
- **The mate term (premise H7-mate-row19: an exhaustive enumeration plus the named premise H-W3-uniform, tested by the organizer).** T_j requires the advice XOR state differences at every row 18..38, so P(T_i and T_j) <= P(T_i) P(S_j | T_i), S_j the event that mate j follows them through row 19. Facts, each checked on real hits: for a hit and every mate on the same claw, the states through row 17 equal the advice's (W12..W17 are the advice words; k4_words fixes A8..A11 and E12..E15); a mate differs from the hit in a3 -> b3 only, so with d = b3 - a3, W3' = W3 + d, W11' = W11 - d and W18' - W18 = Delta(W3, d) = s0(W3 + d) - s0(W3) - d (252 of 252 real mates), while W19' = W19. P is the set of W18 values that admit the advice differences through row 19 (state 17 fixed; the explicit row-18 and row-19 conditions are the predicate P() printed in Appendix D); by enumeration of all 2^32 values |P| = 65,536, and every hit's W18 is in P. A mate with offset d can pass row 19 only if Delta(W3, d) lies in D = P - P (|D| = 9,427,275), i.e. only if the hit's W3 lies in B_d = {W3 : Delta(W3, d) in D, Delta != 0}. The list gives 20 offsets d; over all 2^32 W3, B_d is empty for 14 of them, has 30,256 elements for 2 and 120,832 for 4 (543,840 in all; Appendix D prints the enumeration program). **Pricing under H-W3-uniform.** Let X_i be the number of F8-passing mates of i through row 19; a key has at most 7 other mates, and mate j passes only if W3_i lies in B_{d_j}. Premise H-W3-uniform: given a hit, its W3 is uniform over 2^32. Then E[X_i | T_i] = sum_j P(S_j | T_i) <= sum_j P(W3_i in B_{d_j} | T_i) <= 7 x 120,832 / 2^32 = 1.9693e-04 = eps, and eps/2 = 0.000099 enters the divisor; no independence between mates is assumed. **The organizer test of the premise** (the r39-mate manifest prediction, from the W3 that the 14 organizer-executed runs report inside their hard-asserted digests): of 1,888 hits in 867 carrier clusters, the organizer hits contain 0 W3 values in the union (expected 0.24 under the premise; falsified at 3 or more), and their per-bit chi-square is 24.7 on 32 df (falsified at 62.49, the 99.9% point). **The price without the premise (disclosed, not priced):** a hit-weighted bound needing no premise on W3 treats each cluster as one trial (with mean probability q_c over its hits, the chance that a cluster shows no such W3 cannot exceed 1 - q_c, reached when its hits' events coincide; cluster probabilities free; clusters, distinct carriers, independent); the largest hit-weighted P(W3 in the union | T) consistent with zero events at 99% (maximise sum_c m_c q_c / H subject to prod_c (1 - q_c) >= 0.01) is 0.01716, so eps = 7 x 0.01716 = 0.12015, eps/2 = 0.060077, divisor 1 - 0.133025 and time 94.1648, still under ae2d3c1c's 94.1805. The per-cluster form 4.605 / 867 = 0.00531 and the per-hit form 4.605 / 1,888 = 0.00244 are not used: the first bounds the mean over clusters, not over hits, and the second treats clustered hits as independent. The traced mates: 638 F8-passing mates, first deviation at row 18 for 335 and row 19 for 303, none later; the participant arms of 9054e0c4, re-run with carrier keys (w17/tools/matejoint2.py; 25,221 hits), have none past row 19.

- **Success: second-order Bonferroni over all key hits (counting every hit and counting entries, as a7b383d1 does; credited).** (i) The program tests every W17 key hit of every window: `k4q` (experiments/r39joint_k4.py lines 1042-1057) runs over every survivor lane of every group, and at each key hit compresses every class of the group whose words pass W9, W17 and F8 (lines 1050-1056, 560 per class and 2 x 2,812 per compressed pair, inside the window's counted work and priced in K as key-hit work); after a hit without collision the loops continue, and a window stops early only on a collision (line 804). At most m_max = 1,024 distinct F9 claws are evaluated per window (`k4d`, line 1106). (ii) For a key k with an F8-passing mate in the claw let p'_k = P(U_k | claws), U_k the union of its F8-passing mates' events T_j (Trials); U_k is contained in the key's success, because the program compresses every mate. (iii) Given the hits, the window succeeds with probability at least P(union over hit k of U_k) >= sum over hits of p'_k - sum over hit pairs k < l of P(U_k and U_l) (second-order Bonferroni, for any number H of hits). Each pair term is at most min(p'_k, p'_l) <= (p'_k + p'_l) / 2, whatever the joint law of the tails, so the pair sum is at most sum over hit k of p'_k x (number of other hit keys) / 2. The p'_k are the exact probabilities of the events in the union; a lower bound on them is substituted only after (iv), where each p'_k carries the coefficient q (1 - c2 - drop) > 0. (iv) Average over the hits given the claws (H5): each trial key is hit with probability q = 2^-32; keys of different claws are hit independently; inside one claw W17 = G(a2, kappa, w) + c(claw) with w and c fixed by the claw, so two keys of a claw are hit together exactly when their G values coincide, which the program-independent count sweep/cohit.c measures at 1.336 times the independent pair rate (512 random w, all 3,462,264 keys). Hence E[pair sum | claws] <= sum over k of p'_k [q^2 (n_w - D_c(k)) + q pi_k] / 2, with D_c(k) the trial keys of k's claw and pi_k its expected co-hit partners in that claw. The cross-claw part is q^2 sum over claws c of P_c (m_w - 1) mu_D after averaging the other claws' key counts, which are functions of their own (a0, a1) only and i.i.d. across the claws of a window (H1-screen): since m_w <= m_max by the program, it is at most q^2 (m_max - 1) mu_D P_w for ANY dependence between the number of claws and the tails, with mu_D <= 576,819 (the one-sided 99% bound, rounded up, of the keys per screened F9 claw over 80 batches, 575,302.5 + 2.374 x 637.9). Within a claw, both keys of a pair hit iff their G values coincide. The Bonferroni sum is taken over the sub-collection of hits whose equal-G cluster in the claw has at most 4 keys; a union over fewer events is still a lower bound, and the choice depends on the claw's (w, c) only, not on any tail. For a kept key N_k(w) <= 3, so its pair term is (q/2) p'_k min(N_k(w), 3). Averaged over w (independent of the tails, H5) it is at most (q/2) p'_k pi_max with pi_max = 0.0078, the bound on E[min(N_k, 3)] for every listed key from a third run of 65,536 random w (largest per-key total 267; 7.7446e-03), taken at alpha = 0.001 / (3 x 3,462,264) per key, family-wise at 0.001 over all keys and the three runs (the two earlier runs of 16,384 w give 1.3556e-02 and 1.3355e-02). The left-out hits lose at most q p'_k P(N_k >= 4) of the first-order term, with P(N_k >= 4) <= ln(3 x 3,462,264 / 0.001) / 65,536 = 0.000352 for every key (no N >= 4 for any key in 65,536 w). Participant tools: w15/sweep/cohit2.c (output w15/sweep/cohit2_16384.txt), w15/sweep/cohit3.c (w15/sweep/cohit3_16384.txt and w15/sweep/cohit3_65536.txt), w15/sweep/nf.c (w15/sweep/nf.txt: s0(y) - y has at most 14 preimages, so N_k(w) <= 2,799; not needed by the bound). Both terms are bounded for every key, so they hold whatever the correlation between partner rates and tails across keys. c2 = 2^-32 x 1,023 x 576,819 / 2 + 0.0078 / 2 = 0.068696 + 0.003900 = 0.072596, and the divisor is 1 - c2 - 0.000352 - eps/2 = 1 - 0.072596 - 0.000352 - 0.000099 = 1 - 0.073047 (the mate term above; (1 - a)(1 - b) >= 1 - a - b). No moment of the window size, no correlation and no allowance enters. Over windows, E[q P_w] >= E[n_w] q (1 - eps/2) p_entry, n_w the trial entries of the window and p_entry the entry tail weighted by trial entries (H2-entries). (v) Windows are independent (fresh first blocks): P(no success) <= product over windows of (1 - P(window success)) <= exp(-lambda). No hit is selected or ordered; every hit enters symmetrically; the bound holds for any dependence between the tails of different hits. Hence lambda = B x G x 10701.9 x 2^-32 x 2^-74.4594 x (1 - 0.073047) = -ln 0.61 + 2^-40, set in `k4_budget`; success 0.39. The divisor costs 0.1094 bit. (vi) Real W17 hits at probability 2^-32 were observed: the 48 windows had 37 key hits against 38.58 expected over all 200 groups (dispersion chi-square 34.35 on 47 df); of them, 3 F8-passing mates were compressed against 6.85 expected (Poisson P = 0.09, adverse and not significant; disclosed).
- **The cap does not bind (H6, screened whole-window bound; ae2d3c1c's method, credited, on 124 windows).** The cap is set from the measured totals of whole screened windows: a window's total is the shipped counter `m.o` over `Attack.run_window()` (every screen draw and discard, the base walk, the k4d gate and insertion, every pass, every survivor and key-hit charge). Sample: ae2d3c1c's 60 pre-declared windows (802000-802059, Appendix B) and this entry's 64 (802060-802123, declared before running, Appendix C), all attack path with the screen on and k4 on; this entry's harness reproduces ae2d3c1c's row for 802000 exactly. Mean 589,661,031.7, s.d. 5,673,399.6. H6 model: the screened window totals are i.i.d. over windows and the normal-theory Student-t and chi-square bounds hold. One-sided 99.75% bound on the mean, t(123, 0.9975) = 2.8586: 591,117,427; on the s.d., chi-square(123, 0.0025) = 83.532: 6,884,434.4; jointly 99.5%. Cap per window 10,369 x 57,012.41 = 591,161,679.29: margin 44,252.29 operations per window. Chebyshev on the sum over B = 98,778,303,628,521,972,432,897 windows bounds the probability that the cap binds before B windows by s^2 / (B x margin^2) = 2.46e-19, below the 2^-40 slack inside lambda. The import assertion also checks K >= the panel mean per claw, 10,342.68.
- **The claw cap never binds in the measured windows.** At most 959 distinct F9 claws were evaluated in any of the 124 screened windows (969 in 0b62ed88's 48 unscreened windows) and at most 11 in the organizer windows, below m_max = 1,024, so every k4d call there took the same branch with the same charge as without the cap. The claw factor in the unscreened trial count is the sample mean of min(m_w, 1,024) over the 48 windows; it equals the printed F9 mean because no window reached the cap (maximum 969), and its s.e. is the one carried into the trial bound. **The last window.** The cap is checked between windows; one window's k4 work is at most 1,024 x (143,633 + 62,400 x (5,215 + 49,472)) operations by the cap (every lane a survivor with 8 classes and a key hit), and the whole screened window total was at most 605,480,625 operations in the 124 windows; even 1,000 times that plus the k4 bound keeps one window under 2^42 operations, 2^42 / 2,812 compressions, which is added to the total charged work (Section 5) and to the program's time assertion.

## 9. Advice construction and preprocessing (H3)
As in w13 Section 9: the pair of 5f8e6192, chosen among 93 candidate pairs; 93 x 2^36 = 2^42.5392 constructions plus 93 x 14 x 2^24 = 2^34.35 screens, 2^42.545 in all, declared as preprocessing_log2 = 43 and added to the claimed time. The organizer experiment runs the fibre search on the shipped pair (g16_fibre_size = 2, g17_fibre_size = 1, fibre_dfs_ops = 1,944) and the 256-candidate slice (advice_slice_hits = 1, ops_per_cand = 411). The list is built at import inside K4_SETUP; the choice of the fibre is a one-time offline search: about 7,000 fibres scored (at most 2^36 operations), five enumerated exhaustively by enum15 (per fibre 2^32 F11 tests of about 20 operations, 2^36.3, plus the real two-message trail at four points on at most 1.8 x 10^8 F10-passing solutions at about 10^3 operations each, 2^39.4; five fibres 2^41.8), their F8 counts on about 950 real claws each (9.7 x 10^6 entries x 50 operations per claw, 2^38.7 each, 2^41.0 for five) and one window per fibre: at most 2^42.6 operations, 2^31.1 compressions in all (EST from the tools' loop counts), against the 2^41.1 compressions left between the 2^42.545 of the advice and the declared 2^43.

## 10. Premises, and the limits of their evidence
- **H1-screen (new, MODEL, declared heuristic; price-setting).** Under the screened chaining-value and window law of the shipped program (S <= 5, KCAP = 679, DTRY = 8,192, KTRY = 32; production window 2^26 walk evaluations): (i) the distinct claws per window have mean 57,012.41 (the 124-window panel mean of Appendices B and C, s.d. 214.29), the unit C_W of B and of the cap; (ii) [not used by this entry: the trials are measured on screened windows, Section 7]; (iii) kept chaining values are independent across windows; the (a0, a1) of the distinct F9 claws of a window are i.i.d., independent of the chaining value and of the number of claws, and a claw's trial-key count is a function of its (a0, a1) only (W8..W11, hence F8, do not depend on the chaining value); the W17 claw constants (w, c) are uniform and independent of (a0, u), as H5 uses. In this entry (ii) is replaced by the measurement of Section 7 on 80 screened windows: 10701.9 F8-passing entries per distinct claw (one-sided 99%); one-way ANOVA of the 10,000 screened claws' entry counts over their 80 windows: F = 1.175 on 79 and 9,920 df (keys F = 1.242); first 125 claws against the rest on all F9 claws of windows 802000 and 802001: 677,197.7 and 676,356.3 entries against 681,901.6 and 683,853.0 (Welch z = -0.69, -1.17). Support (participant-run, paired, same seeds on both builds; 16 seed pairs, 2^24 walk evaluations, harness winmeasure_rival.py; N = F8-passing listed entries and K = distinct keys among them over the four diagnostic groups 0, 50, 100, 150 of k4f, per distinct claw C): unscreened N/C 106.91, K/C 98.56; screened N/C 111.16, K/C 102.24; paired N/C change +0.0552 bit (s.e. 0.0459). Distinct F9 claws per window: 907.17 (s.d. 25.68) in the 60 screened 2^26 windows against 898.62 in the 48 unscreened ones. This probe concerned the base's trial premise (ii), which this entry does not use (its trials are measured on screened windows, Section 7).
- **H1-ops.** The constants of Sections 3 and 5; the pass is a constant of the program; the screen charges 4 + 183 per draw and 3 per discarded draw.
- **H2-entries (MODEL premise of this entry; screened scope).** p_entry >= 2^-74.4783 for an F8-passing listed entry of class 01 drawn uniformly over all trial (window, claw, entry) triples of the attack, windows drawn under the screened law and weighted by their trial count, in a claw passing F9 with W17 hit: the lower of the 14-run organizer pooled and class-01 means of r39-mate (Section 8; 2^-74.4594 and 2^-74.4783), rounded down. A mean of organizer-executed runs, carried to the screened window law and the whole attack, not a lower confidence bound. ae2d3c1c's H2-transfer (2^-74.3238, keys, designated mate) is cited only as the keys value; arm J (2^-74.3828) is participant-run support. Model, stated plainly: the SMC carrier sees a window only through its claws' (a0, a1).
- **H3-advice-construction.** As in w13; for every listed entry of the new fibre both messages follow the advice trail through step 15 (enum15 on all entries; the organizer run on one entry of every group).
- **H5-group-independence (screened-window scope).** For the windows of the screened law: windows independent (fresh first blocks, each drawn and screened independently); trials are F8-passing entries, at least 10701.9 per distinct claw (measured on screened windows, Section 7); W17 is shared by the mates of a key, so hits are counted on keys; each listed key's W17 event has probability 2^-32 in each claw; events of different claws are independent. Within a claw, two keys hit together iff G(a2, kappa, w) = s0(a2 + w) - (a2 + w) + kappa coincide. Let N_k(w) be the number of other listed keys with G equal to key k's at the claw's w, and pi_k = E_w[N_k(w)]. Measured over all 3,462,264 listed keys on two independent sets of 16,384 random w: mean pi 1.07e-3, largest per-key estimate 4.6e-3; per-(key, w) counts on the second set: N = 1 in 60,723,478 cases, N = 2 in 37,173, N = 3 in 40, N >= 4 in none of 5.67e10. At the w of 2,000 real F9 claws of 0b62ed88's unscreened program: mean pi 1.0825e-3, largest per-(key, w) N = 3 (w15/critic_final/cohit_real.c, cohit_real_2000.txt; w and u at all 43,134 real claws in wreal.py, wreal.txt). The claw's w contains -cv5 additively, so it is uniform and independent of (a0, u) under H1-screen. Hits whose equal-G cluster in the claw has more than 4 keys are left out of the second-order sum; for every kept key N_k <= 3, and E[min(N_k, 3)] <= 0.0078 for every key (a run of 65,536 random w; family-wise at 0.001 over all keys and the three runs). Left-out hits cost at most P(N_k >= 4) <= ln(3 x 3,462,264 / 0.001) / 65,536 = 0.000352 per key in the first-order term (no N >= 4 for any key in 65,536 w). Both bounds hold for every key, so the within-claw term holds whatever the relation between a key's partner rate and its tail. The claw's W17 constants (w, c) are independent of the mates' tail events, as for the hit events themselves. 37 real 2^-32 key hits were observed against 38.58 expected (Section 7).
- **H7-mate-row19 (new; named premise H-W3-uniform).** Given a hit, its W3 is uniform over 2^32 (H-W3-uniform). With the exhaustive enumeration of Section 7 (Appendix D: a mate with offset d can follow the advice through row 19 only if W3 lies in B_d, |B_d| <= 120,832), the expected number of a hit's other F8-passing mates that do so is at most eps = 7 x 120,832 / 2^32 = 1.9693e-04. Organizer test: the r39-mate manifest predicts at most two of the 1,888 hits' W3 in the union of the B_d (observed 0) and a per-bit chi-square below 62.49 (observed 24.7). Without the premise, the strict 99% cluster bound gives eps 0.12015 and time 94.1648 (disclosed, not priced). Limitation: the r39-mate hits come from the replica's start-state and claw law, one listed entry per batch; the test is carried to the attack's screened claws as the entries tail is (H2-entries).
- **H6-cap-completion.** Section 7: the screened whole-window bound, a model-based 99.75% bound on the mean (and on the s.d.) of the screened window work under the stated window-distribution model.
- **H-implicit-distinct-key-dispersion.** Tested in the organizer run at a scaled event over all keys of four groups in every F9 claw (Section 11).
- **Limits of the evidence.** The cap sample is 124 screened windows of the shipped attack path on public seeds (ae2d3c1c's 60 and this entry's 64); the trial count is 10,000 claws of 80 screened windows run by this entry: participant-run. The mate term's data are organizer-executed (r39-mate-01..14); the participant re-runs of arms M and J are support. The r39-mate hits come from the replica's start-state law with the claw model for (a0, a1), not from screened claws; their W3 count is carried to the attack's screened claws as the entries tail is (H2-entries). The organizer run counts F8-passing keys and their scaled dispersion on four fixed groups of the 200 (22 claws); it is a spot test at probability 2^-7 and does not establish independence of the 2^-32 events over all groups and all windows, which remains the premise H5. The tail replica the organizer runs samples the advice distribution; the entries tail rests on the 14 organizer-executed r39-mate runs (the lower of their pooled and class-01 means), with arm J as participant-run support. The memory claim is a peak over phases. No full collision has been executed; every experiment is a component test.

## 11. Experiments (organizer sandbox; every organizer-run value is hard-asserted by the program)
- `r39-transplant-claw`, trial 0: the advice collides under 39 steps; the advice-construction checks of Section 9; and for the sample entry of each of the 200 groups at the advice point: the rule holds, W9 = advice W9 + 0x05cefde0, W16 one value, both messages follow the advice trail through step 16 and message 1 the advice states from A[8], E[12] (200 of 200). Every further trial: a random chaining value and claw-free (a0, u) with a listed entry of the fibre: transplant states, W1 = u and W16 - g = F(u) - F(a0).
- `r39k4-window-small`, trials 0-3: windows of 2^21 evaluations, check mode, k4 on for every F9 claw (7, 11, 4, 1 claws). Every claw asserts W9 = C9 + HD - a1 = W9 of a listed entry and W16 = g. The pass runs over all 62,400 lanes. Asserted tuples (claws, F9, 0, pass lanes, survivors, key hits, k4 ops, total ops): (233,7,0,436800,2,0,1019221,11504962), (222,11,0,624000,5,0,1454268,13875066), (256,4,0,249600,2,0,584630,13031225), (232,1,0,62400,0,0,144113,11245985). Each k4 ops value is (evaluated F9 claws, pass lanes / 62,400) x (143,633 + 480), plus 12 per repeated F9 claw (the dedupe lookup), plus 10,430 for its 2 real survivors; 13,126 for its 5 real survivors; 8,178 for its 2 real survivors. Each trial emits k4_setup = 1,107,473,556.
  - The four asserted windows run with the screen off (`screen=0`; the k4 path is the same code with the screen on or off), so their tuples are 0b62ed88's.
  - Pass-off control: trials 0 and 1 are re-run with k4 off; claws and F9 equal, ops_off = ops - k4_ops.
  - Screened window (trial 0, same seed, screen on as on the attack path): asserted that the window is not skipped, the kept chaining value has S <= 5, every draw is charged 187 operations (kept) or 190 (discarded), and the discarded-draw count equals the number of draws with S > 5. On the organizer seed of trial 0: 12 draws, 11 discarded, kept S = 1, (claws, F9, total ops) = (258, 1, 10,371,107). No new output key.
  - Planted check on the first F9 claw of each window, for each of the 200 groups: the key is found and its counted cost is asserted.
  - Key dispersion over all entries of every 50th group (4 groups), all F9 claws: per claw D = keys with an entry in F8, K = those whose W17 x 2654435761 mod 2^32 has its top 7 bits zero (probability 2^-7). Asserted per trial (sum D, sum K, Pearson, claws): (59,256, 437, 6.5188, 7); (67,492, 518, 7.9839, 10); (17,882, 142, 0.7772, 4); (1,872, 7, 4.0067, 1). Pooled 146,502 key events, 1,104 hits against 1144.5 expected (z = -1.20), Pearson 19.29 on 22 claws. Acceptance region, asserted on the sums: sum D >= 96,821, |sum K - sum D/128| within 2.576 s.d., Pearson < 40.29 (99% quantile, 22 dof).
- `r39-tail-01..14` (not in this manifest): w13's replica (experiments/r39tail.py in earlier entries) is the first part of experiments/r39mate.py, byte-identical but for its final main-guard line, because the verifier admits only the files that the manifest runs; trial 0 of every r39-mate run calls its verify_smc_stats(QDECL), so the replica's calibration (c18 = 206) and its 14-run table with the asserted bounds are executed in every run.
- `r39-mate-01..14` (new, experiments/r39mate.py; all 14 in the manifest, organizer-executed): the unchanged replica; one uniform listed entry per batch of 2,048 lanes (4 kappa groups per run drawn proportional to size and asserted against the rule's enumeration), the lanes' W8, W9 the replica's own draws; 6 chunks x 80 batches. Every collision verified by the replica's own verify(), its class counted, its chaining value and message recovered and reproduced by k4_words, its W3 recorded; every F8-passing mate of the same key recompressed on the same claw and traced row by row. Predictions on the reported W3 (checked from the observations, not asserted in code): over the 14 runs at most two hits have W3 in the union of the B_d of Appendix D (expected 0.24 if W3 were uniform; falsified at 3 or more), and the per-bit chi-square of the hits' W3 is below 62.49 on 32 df (the 99.9% point); observed 0 and 24.7. Hard-asserted: the prediction (no mate past row 19), the group sizes, the replica's calibration and table, and each run's replay digest (sha256 of the observations, the 12-hex prefixes in the per-run table of Section 8). Totals: 1,888 hits (class 01: 466), 638 F8-passing mates, first deviation at row 18 for 335 and row 19 for 303, none later.
- Run by this entry (participant-run; tools not in the package, outputs cited): the 80 screened 2^26 windows (802000-802015 with k4 off, which leaves the walk and its claws unchanged: window 802000 run both ways gives the same claws and reproduces ae2d3c1c's Appendix B row; 802060-802123 on the attack path; tools/win17.py, win17b.py) and the 10,000-claw entries count (trials17b.py); the rows-18-19 enumeration (|P| = 65,536, D = P - P, the 20 mate offsets, the bad W3 counts per offset; row19_proof/pset.c, deltas.c, row19x.c, rate.c, re-checked by tools/row19gate.c on the organizer's hit W3 values; row19x.c and adv.h are printed in Appendix D); the re-runs of 9054e0c4's mate arms with carrier keys (tools/matejoint2.py) and the cluster analysis (tools/analyze_cl.py), disclosed as support.
- Local seed sets, run by this entry with the same program and code path: 11 sets of 4 windows with seeds fixed before any run (sha256 of `w15-dispersion|setNN|i`), 138 claws, 6,693 hits against 6675.6 expected (z = +0.21), Pearson 126.68 on 138 degrees of freedom; the largest set value is z = +1.43. On the organizer seeds the largest per-claw |z| is 2.00.
- Run by 0b62ed88 and ae2d3c1c (CITED; tools not in this package): 48 full windows (Appendix A); 2,000 unscreened claws (their trial count, not used here); the exhaustive and end-to-end checks of Section 2; the memory audit of Section 6; the walk-kernel generator on 300 chaining values (Section 6). Run by ae2d3c1c for the screened program (CITED, participant-run): the 60 screened windows of Appendix B; the paired 2^24 yield probe of H1-screen. Linux (WSL) wall time of each experiment of this package in the organizer form, measured by this entry over three passes (ae2d3c1c's figures were of another machine): r39-mate 6.6-7.2 s; r39-transplant-claw 0.7-0.8 s; r39k4-window-small 6.9-6.9 s; every run at most 7.2 s.

## Appendix D. The rows-18-19 enumeration (participant-run; row19_proof/row19x.c and adv.h, verbatim)

P(w) below is the explicit set of conditions: with the advice states through row 17 fixed (adv.h, generated from the replica's advice trace), W18 = w must give the advice's XOR differences of A and E after row 18 (TA22, TE22), and the row-19 modular E difference must be one of +-2^19 +-2^5 with a matching A difference. B_d is the set of W3 with Delta(W3, d) = s0(W3 + d) - s0(W3) - d a nonzero element of D = P - P. Output (row19x.out, sha256 88005a11...): |P| = 65,536, |D| = 9,427,275; per offset, the size of B_d as in Section 7.

```c
/* row19x.c: exhaustive check that no mate of a colliding entry can follow the advice through row 19.
   (1) P = {W18 : rows 18-19 admit the advice differences, states through row 17 = advice}, by enumeration of 2^32.
   (2) D = P - P (bitset over 2^32).
   (3) For every mate offset d in delta_set.bin (all b3 - a3 over listed entries of one key) and every W3 in 2^32:
       Delta = s0(W3+d) - s0(W3) - d (the mate's W18 minus the hit's). A mate can pass row 19 only if Delta in D.
   Counts Delta == 0 separately (then rows 18 coincide and row 19 is decided by W19). */
#include <stdio.h>
#include <stdlib.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <string.h>
#include "adv.h"
typedef uint32_t u32; typedef uint64_t u64;
#define ROR(x,k) (((x)>>(k))|((x)<<(32-(k))))
static inline u32 S0(u32 x){return ROR(x,2)^ROR(x,13)^ROR(x,22);}
static inline u32 S1(u32 x){return ROR(x,6)^ROR(x,11)^ROR(x,25);}
static inline u32 s0(u32 x){return ROR(x,7)^ROR(x,18)^(x>>3);}
static inline u32 CH(u32 e,u32 f,u32 g){return (e&f)^(~e&g);}
static inline u32 MJ(u32 a,u32 b,u32 c){return (a&b)^(a&c)^(b&c);}
static int P(u32 w){
  u32 ex=AX[18]+EX[18]+S1(EX[21])+CH(EX[21],EX[20],EX[19])+K18+w, ey=AY[18]+EY[18]+S1(EY[21])+CH(EY[21],EY[20],EY[19])+K18+w;
  u32 ax=ex-AX[18]+S0(AX[21])+MJ(AX[21],AX[20],AX[19]), ay=ey-AY[18]+S0(AY[21])+MJ(AY[21],AY[20],AY[19]);
  if((ax^ay)!=TA22||(ex^ey)!=TE22) return 0;
  u32 fx=AX[19]+EX[19]+S1(ex)+CH(ex,EX[21],EX[20])+K19, fy=AY[19]+EY[19]+S1(ey)+CH(ey,EY[21],EY[20])+K19, DE=fy-fx;
  u32 gx=-AX[19]+S0(ax)+MJ(ax,AX[21],AX[20]), gy=-AY[19]+S0(ay)+MJ(ay,AY[21],AY[20]);
  if(DE+gy-gx) return 0;
  return DE==(u32)(-(1u<<19)+(1u<<5))||DE==(u32)((1u<<19)+(1u<<5))||DE==(u32)((1u<<19)-(1u<<5))||DE==(u32)(-(1u<<19)-(1u<<5));
}
static u32 L[1<<17];
int main(){
  int nL=0; for(u64 W=0;W<(1ull<<32);W++){u32 w=(u32)W;if(P(w))L[nL++]=w;}
  printf("|P| = %d\n",nL); fflush(stdout);
  u64*D=calloc(1ull<<26,8); if(!D){printf("alloc\n");return 2;}
  for(int i=0;i<nL;i++){u32 a=L[i];for(int j=0;j<nL;j++){u32 d=L[j]-a;D[d>>6]|=1ull<<(d&63);}}
  u64 nd=0;for(u64 i=0;i<(1ull<<26);i++)nd+=__builtin_popcountll(D[i]);
  printf("|D| = |P-P| = %llu (2^%.3f)\n",nd,__builtin_log2((double)nd)); fflush(stdout);
  /* low-residue filter mod 2^23 */
  u64*F=calloc(1u<<17,8);for(u64 i=0;i<(1ull<<26);i++)if(D[i]){u64 m=D[i];while(m){int b=__builtin_ctzll(m);m&=m-1;u32 d=(u32)(i*64+b);F[(d&0x7fffff)>>6]|=1ull<<(d&63);}}
  u64 nf=0;for(int i=0;i<(1<<17);i++)nf+=__builtin_popcountll(F[i]);printf("residues mod 2^23 covered: %llu of 8388608\n",nf);fflush(stdout);
  FILE*f=fopen("delta_set.bin","rb");u32 ds[64];int nds=(int)fread(ds,4,64,f);fclose(f);
  printf("mate offsets d: %d\n",nds);
  u64 tot_in=0,tot_zero=0;
  for(int k=0;k<nds;k++){u32 d=ds[k];u64 in=0,zero=0;u32 ex_in=0,ex_zero=0;
    for(u64 W=0;W<(1ull<<32);W++){u32 w=(u32)W;u32 Dl=s0(w+d)-s0(w)-d;
      if(!Dl){if(!zero)ex_zero=w;zero++;continue;}
      if(!((F[(Dl&0x7fffff)>>6]>>(Dl&63))&1))continue;
      if((D[Dl>>6]>>(Dl&63))&1){if(!in)ex_in=w;in++;}}
    printf("d=%08x  Delta in D (nonzero): %llu%s  Delta==0: %llu%s\n",d,in,in?"":"",zero,"");
    if(in)printf("   e.g. W3=%08x\n",ex_in); if(zero)printf("   e.g. W3=%08x (Delta 0)\n",ex_zero);
    fflush(stdout);tot_in+=in;tot_zero+=zero;}
  printf("TOTAL over all d and all W3: Delta in D\{0}: %llu ; Delta == 0: %llu\n",tot_in,tot_zero);
  return 0;}
```
